🌿 Life lately has been hard... and holy.

I’ve walked through heartbreak, unexpected motherhood (again), job loss, and watching things I poured myself into — courses, devotionals, subscription boxes — completely flop.

But through it all, God has gently led me back to what He originally called me to: writing.

Not writing to build a business.
Not writing to keep up.
Just writing to bloom where He planted me.

So that’s what I’m doing.

Fiction, non-fiction, devotionals, journaling, blogging. Writing with joy again. And somehow, that feels like coming home.

If you’re walking through a season of redirection too, I’d love for you to read my latest post. It’s raw, real, and full of hope. Maybe it’ll speak to you like it did to me while writing it.

Being an author is hard. Being an author is scary. Putting your writing out there and asking others to critique it can lead to insecurity, hurt, and a myriad of emotions. 

The important thing to remember is when developing your thick skin, don't forget to let yourself feel. Breathe in the criticism, both constructive and unkind. Breathe in the positives of those who love your writing and feel inspired by it. Dig deep into the negatives you've received to meditate on what might need to be improved. It takes both to evolve and improve as a writer. 

It's not always easy – you won't always be somebody's cup of tea, and neither will your writing. But if you are doing what you feel you are called to do and trust in the process, you will forge forward and get your words out into the world, no matter how others might feel about your gift or your talent. Don't give up, believe in yourself, do it for those who will truly be helped by it and are meant to hold your story in their hands. 🤲🏼 📖 😌
